analysisMethod: rankings converted to category weights in the Army's AoA, Tab I, 'Ground Combat Vehicle Affordability Strategy' (p. 33 fn 1)
inclusionReason: the basis of CBO's primary-metric weights (pp. 33–34)
instrument: ranking of the vehicle's most important characteristics (p. 33)

limitations.impact: the rankings → Army weights step cannot be checked; the Army weights → CBO weights step is an exact division and can be checked against Table A-1
limitations.statement: Only the second half of the derivation is public. CBO's four weights are the Army's four retained weights renormalised — 0.20/0.15/0.10/0.05 over their sum of 0.50 gives 0.40/0.30/0.20/0.10 exactly (Table A-1, p. 34) — but how the Army turned soldiers' rankings into those weights is in the AoA's Tab I, which is not public

pointer.custodian: Department of the Army (instrument and responses, not public); CBO (reported weights)

reviewers.name: Department of the Army (analysis of alternatives)

scopeOfValidity.builtToAnswer: Which characteristics of a fighting vehicle matter most to soldiers who have deployed with combat brigades?
scopeOfValidity.intendedUse: set the Army's AoA category weights

selectionRule: soldiers who had been deployed with combat brigades in Iraq, Afghanistan, Kosovo, or Bosnia (p. 33)
title: Soldier ranking of the characteristics that matter most in a fighting vehicle — the source of the Army's AoA category weights
